title: Ines and the Parish
premise: Rosalind Delacroix, a night-shift dispatcher for a New Orleans taxi company, is hired to find Ines Marchand, a parish archivist who vanished three weeks ago. The case turns strange when Ines's recovered diary keeps receiving entries dated after her disappearance—entries in handwriting that isn't hers. Following the diary's clues, Rosalind uncovers a thirty-year-old cover-up: Ines witnessed the drowning of a child during a church flood and was paid by prominent families to stay silent about who was responsible. The final diary entries are Ines's own coded confession, written before she staged her disappearance to force the truth into the open. Rosalind finds her alive on a shrimp boat in Barataria Bay, and together they let the tide—and the truth—give up what it took.
about_author: Hazel Quintana spent six years answering phones at a 24-hour cab dispatch before turning to fiction, a job that taught her how much of a city reveals itself after midnight. She writes mysteries about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Last Fare Logged
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A lawyer hires Rosalind to locate Ines Marchand, missing since Mardi Gras week. Rosalind pulls Ines's last taxi ride from dispatch records—a fare to the flooded parish of St. Brigid at 3 a.m., logged but never invoiced. Emotional beat: cautious curiosity; Rosalind treats it as just another file to close.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Searching Ines's apartment, Rosalind finds her diary—its final pages continue past the disappearance date, in different ink and a shakier hand. The entries reference 'the water debt' and name no one. Emotional beat: unease deepening into obsession as Rosalind realizes this is no ordinary missing person's case.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Drawer
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At St. Brigid's parish office, Rosalind meets Father Aubert and discovers Ines's filing drawer emptied except for one misfiled baptismal record from 1994—the year of the flood. Emotional beat: first real fear; someone else has been here recently, and the dust tells Rosalind when.

chapters.title: What the Families Paid For
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Following the 1994 record, Rosalind interviews Odile Fontenot, matriarch of a shipping family whose son drowned that year—or so the record says. Odile's alibi is polished, rehearsed, thirty years old. Emotional beat: Rosalind recognizes the texture of a lie she's heard a thousand times on dispatch calls.

chapters.title: Night Shift Confessions
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind with flashback threads. A retired dispatcher, Manny, drinks with Rosalind and admits he drove Ines's mother home the night of the flood—saw a second child in the car, a girl who wasn't Ines. Emotional beat: grief and loyalty colliding; Manny begs Rosalind to drop it, revealing how deep the silence runs.

chapters.title: The Hand That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A graphologist confirms the post-disappearance diary entries belong to an older woman. Cross-referencing handwriting samples, Rosalind lands on Odile herself—writing Ines's diary to control what investigators would find. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the case flips from search to counter-move.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The diary's coded references match tide charts and a derelict boathouse in Barataria Bay. Rosalind stakes out the boathouse and spots fresh supplies—someone is feeding whoever hides there. Emotional beat: rising tension; Rosalind realizes Ines may be alive, hiding, and watching her back.

chapters.title: The Water Debt
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Confronted with evidence, Odile confesses partially: her family paid Ines to bury the truth that the Fontenot boy drowned fleeing a drunk driver—Odile's own daughter. But Ines kept a copy of everything. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; Rosalind sees the found family Ines built among the guilty and the grieving alike.

chapters.title: Barataria
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Climax. Rosalind follows the supply run to a shrimp boat and finds Ines alive, having staged her vanishing to force the parish's reckoning. Odile's enforcer arrives to burn the evidence; a storm, a standoff, and Ines's calm testimony turn him back. Emotional beat: terror giving way to fierce recognition between two women who live invisibly.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Resolution. Ines comes forward publicly; the Fontenot daughter surrenders, and the parish holds its first honest memorial for the drowned boy. Ines offers Rosalind partnership in a discreet investigations practice. Emotional beat: quiet belonging—Rosalind, the perpetual night-shift ghost, finally lets herself be seen.
